100.name: CONTINUE
100.description: Server received request headers and client should proceed to send the request body (e.g. for POST requests) To have a server check the request headers, a client must send `Expect: 100-continue` as a header in its initial request and receive a `100-Continue` status code in the response from the server before sending the body. If the client receives an error code such as `403 Forbidden` or `405 Method Not Allowed` then it should not send the body. The response `417 Expectation Failed` indicates that the request should be repeated without the `Expect` header.

101.name: SWITCHING_PROTOCOLS
101.description: The client has asked the server to switch protocols and the server has agreed to do so

102.name: PROCESSING
102.description: A WebDAV request may contain many sub-requests that may take a long time to complete. This status code indicates that the server has received and is processing the request, but no response is available yet. This prevents the client from timing out assuming the request was lost.

103.name: EARLY_HINTS
103.description: Used to return some response headers before the final HTTP message

200.name: OK
200.description: Standard response for successful HTTP requests. The actual response depends on the actual method used. For GET requests, the response will contain an entity corresponding to the requested resource. For POST requests, the response will contain an entity describing or containing the result of the action.

201.name: CREATED
201.description: The request has been accepted, and a new resource has been created

202.name: ACCEPTED
202.description: The request has been accepted, but the processing has not been completed. The request may or may not be eventually acted upon and may be disallowed when processing.

203.name: NON_AUTHORITATIVE_INFORMATION
203.description: The server is a transforming proxy (e.g. a Web Accelerator) that received a `200 OK` from its origin, but is returning a modified version of its response.

204.name: NO_CONTENT
204.description: The server processed the request successfully and is not returning any content

205.name: RESET_CONTENT
205.description: The server successfully processed the request, asks that the client reset its document view, and is not returning any content

206.name: PARTIAL_CONTENT
206.description: The server is delivering only part of the content due to a range header set by the client. The range header is used by HTTP clients to enable resuming of interrupted downloads, or split a download into multiple simultaneous streams.

207.name: MULTI_STATUS
207.description: The message body that follows is by default an XML message and can contain a number of separate response codes, depending on the number of sub-requests

208.name: ALREADY_REPORTED
208.description: The members of a DAV binding have already been enumerated in a preceding part of the (multi-status) response, and are not being included again

226.name: IM_USED
226.description: The server has fulfilled a request for the resource, and the response is a representation of the result of one or more instance-manipulations applied to the current instance.

300.name: MULTIPLE_CHOICES
300.description: Indicates multiple options for the resource from which the client may choose (via agent-driven content negotiation) For example, this could be used to - present multiple video formats options. - list files with different filename extensions.

301.name: MOVED_PERMANENTLY
301.description: This and all future request should be redirected to the given URL

302.name: FOUND
302.description: Tells the client to look at another URL.

303.name: SEE_OTHER
303.description: The response to this request can be found under another URL using the GET method. When receiving in response to a POST/PUT/DELETE request, the client should presume the server has received the data and should issue a GET request to the given URL

304.name: NOT_MODIFIED
304.description: Indicates that the resource has not been modified since the version specified by the request headers `if-Modified-Since` or `if-None-Match`. In such a case, there is no need to retransmit the resource since the client still has a previously-downloaded copy.

305.name: USE_PROXY
305.description: The requested resource is only available through a proxy, the address for which is provided in the response. NOTE: for security reasons, many HTTP clients (like Mozilla Firefox and Internet Explorer) do not obey this status code

306.name: SWITCH_PROXY
306.description: No longer used. Originally meant - Subsequent requests should used the specified proxy

307.name: TEMPORARY_REDIRECT
307.description: In this case, the request should be repeated with another URI. However, future requests should still use this URI.

308.name: PERMANENT_REDIRECT
308.description: This and all future requests should be directed to the given URI

400.name: BAD_REQUEST
400.description: The server cannot or will not process the request due to an apparent client error (e.g. malformed request syntax, size too large etc)

401.name: UNAUTHORIZED
401.description: Similar to `403 Forbidden`, but specifically for use when authentication is required and has failed or has not yet been provided. The response must include a WWW-Authenticate header field containing a challenge applicable to the requested resource. `401` semantically means **Unauthorized**, the user does not have valid authentication credentials for the target resource.

402.name: PAYMENT_REQUIRED
402.description: Not widely used, reserved for future use. The original intention was that this code might be used as part of some form of digital cash or micro-payment scheme. But that has not yet happened.

403.name: FORBIDDEN
403.description: The request contained valid data and was understood by the server, but the server is refusing action. This may be due to user not having the necessary permissions for a resource or needing an account of some sort, or attempting a prohibited action (e.g. creating a duplicate record where only one is allowed)

405.name: METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED
405.description: A request method is not supported for the requested resource. e.g. using a GET request to post form-data that requires a POST request

406.name: NOT_ACCEPTABLE
406.description: The requested resource is capable of generating only content not acceptable according to the Accept headers sent in the request

407.name: PROXY_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED
407.description: Client must first authenticate itself with the proxy

408.name: REQUEST_TIMEOUT
408.description: The server timed out waiting for the request

409.name: CONFLICT
409.description: Indicates that the request could not be processed because of a conflict. e.g. edit conflict between multiple simultaneous updates

410.name: GONE
410.description: Indicates that request is no longer available and will never be available again This should be used when a resource has been intentionally removed and the resource should be purged. Upon receiving a `410` request, the client should not request this resource again. Clients such as search engines should remove the resource from their indices. Most general use cases do not require a `410` a `404` is enough.

411.name: LENGTH_REQUIRED
411.description: The request did not specify the length of its content, which is required by the requested resource

412.name: PRECONDITION_FAILED
412.description: The server did not meet one of the preconditions that the requester put on the request header fields

413.name: PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE
413.description: The request is larger than the server is willing or able to process

414.name: URI_TOO_LONG
414.description: The URI provided was too long for the server to process. Often the result of too much data being encoded in a query-string

415.name: UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE
415.description: The request entity has a media type that the server does not support

416.name: RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE
416.description: The client has asked for a portion of the file, but server cannot supply that portion

417.name: EXPECTATION_FAILED
417.description: The server cannot meet the requirements of the `Expect` request-header field

418.name: IM_A_TEAPOT
418.description: This code was an April Fools' joke. Not expected to be implemented by any HTTP server. The RFC specifies this code should be returned by teapots requested to brew coffee.

421.name: MISDIRECTED_REQUEST
421.description: The request was directed at a server that is not able to produce a response

422.name: UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY
422.description: The request was well-formed but was unable to be followed doe to semantic errors

423.name: LOCKED
423.description: The resource that is being accessed is locked

424.name: FAILED_DEPENDENCY
424.description: The request failed because it depends on another request that failed

425.name: TOO_EARLY
425.description: Indicates that the server is unwilling to risk processing a request that might be replayed

426.name: UPGRADE_REQUIRED
426.description: The client should switch to a different protocol such as TLS/1.3 given in the header field

428.name: PRECONDITION_REQUIRED
428.description: The origin server requires the request to be conditional

429.name: TOO_MANY_REQUESTS
429.description: The user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time. Intended for use with rate limiting schemes

431.name: REQUEST_HEADER_FIELDS_TOO_LARGE
431.description: The server is unwilling to process the request because headers are too large

451.name: UNAVAILABLE_FOR_LEGAL_REASONS
451.description: A server operator has received a legal demand to deny access to a resource or to a set of resources that includes the requested resource

500.name: INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
500.description: A generic error message, given when an unexpected condition was encountered and no more specific message is suitable

501.name: NOT_IMPLEMENTED
501.description: This server either does not recognize the request method, or it lacks the ability to fulfill the request.

502.name: BAD_GATEWAY
502.description: The server was acting as a gateway or proxy and received an invalid response from the upstream server.

503.name: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
503.description: The server cannot handle the request (because it is overloaded or down for maintenance). Generally this is a temporary state.

504.name: GATEWAY_TIMEOUT
504.description: The server was acting as a gateway or a proxy and dit not receive a timely response from the upstream server

505.name: HTTP_VERSION_NOT_SUPPORTED
505.description: The server does not support the HTTP protocol version used in the request

506.name: VARIANT_ALSO_NEGOTIATES
506.description: Transparent content negotiation for the request results in a circular reference

507.name: INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE
507.description: The server is unable to store the representation needed to complete the request

508.name: LOOP_DETECTED
508.description: The server detected an infinite loop while processing the request (sent instead of `208 Already reported`)

510.name: NOT_EXTENDED
510.description: Further extensions to the request are required for the server to fulfill it

511.name: NETWORK_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED
511.description: The client needs to authenticate to gain network access Intended for use by intercepting proxies used to control access to the network (e.g. captive portals) used to require agreement to Terms of Service before granting full internet access via a Wi-Fi hotspot.
